agents.note:
US-533 BLOCKED -- BL-030 filed, NO code written, sprint stays 4/6 (US-530/531/532/536 done). NEXT: US-537 (animation-gating) is unaffected and pickable NOW. Do NOT re-dispatch US-533 until Atlas + CIO rule on the two items below.

*** I STOPPED BEFORE WRITING CODE, AND THAT WAS THE WHOLE VALUE OF THE ITERATION. *** Two of the five controls cannot be wired as the ACs are written. I found both by tracing the authorization chain end to end BEFORE implementing -- which is the cheap direction. Had I built first, I would have shipped a green test suite over a toggle that is dead on the Pi, because nothing in the dev-box test kit can see a PolicyKit denial.

B1 (CRITICAL) -- AC-2's eclipse-states-http BOUNCE IS DENIED BY POLKIT. The state server cannot restart itself: it runs User=mcornelison (deploy/eclipse-states-http.service:43), and the manage-units grant in 51-eclipse-service-control.rules:52-68 covers exactly FOUR units -- powerwatch/obd/sync/dashboard -- with states-http absent and the rule ending in explicit default-deny. unit_manifest.py:131-135 likewise gives it NO kioskVerbs. So `systemctl restart eclipse-states-http.service` returns "Interactive authentication required" and the auto-rotate toggle becomes a SILENT NO-OP -- the exact failure AC-4 forbids and the entire reason the F-126 band exists.

THE PART THAT MAKES IT A BLOCKER RATHER THAN A PATCH: the withholding is DELIBERATE. unit_manifest.py:18-20 states the narrowness as a safety property -- "a compromised kiosk must not be able to reach the splash, THE STATE SERVER or the safe-shutdown guard." So AC-2 contradicts a different Atlas ruling. Atlas-vs-Atlas is not mine to break (PM Rule 10).

THREE PATHS (full trade-off table in BL-030): (1) a new 52- polkit file granting restart-only on that one unit -- follows the "add a SECOND rule file rather than widening this one" precedent from 50-...rules:19-21, and leaves kioskVerbs empty so the kiosk's own POST /service still refuses it (OS layer opens, app layer holds); costs one layer of defense-in-depth. (2) SELF-EXIT bounce -- zero privilege, exploits the unit's existing Restart=on-failure + RestartSec=2; but systemd's default 5-starts-in-10s limit means FIVE FAST TOGGLES WEDGE THE UNIT INTO `failed` and the dashboard goes dark until a manual reset-failed, so it needs StartLimitIntervalSec=0, i.e. a unit-file change + deploy anyway -- which was its only advantage over (1). (3) RECOMMENDED -- resolve carouselConfig PER REQUEST and delete the need for a restart entirely.

WHY #3, AND WHY I AM CONFIDENT DESPITE RECOMMENDING AGAINST THE STATED REMEDY: the precedent is already INSIDE the same function. _injectHtml (states_http_server.py:466-488) resolves __DEPLOY_VERSION__ (US-501) and __DISPLAY_SETTINGS__ (US-532) per request, each with a comment explaining that a construction-cached value is stale by exactly one deploy/save. carouselConfig (US-506) is the LAST resolved-at-construction value left in that method and it has the identical failure mode. Paths 1 and 2 both spend real safety margin to preserve a cache that #3 simply removes; #3 needs no privilege, no unit change, no downtime window, no start-limit hazard, and auto-rotate then applies on a page reload the UI can trigger itself. It is still Atlas's call because it overrides his stated GAP 1 remedy -- but note it does NOT weaken honesty: the row keeps a truthful "applies on reload" label, and US-532's deliberate STORED-vs-RUNNING non-parity stays meaningful.

B2 (HIGH) -- pi.alerts.audioAlerts HAS ZERO CONSUMERS. It exists in exactly two places: a default (obdii/config/loader.py:142) and a validator (common/config/overlay.py:121). AlertManager takes visualAlerts + logAlerts ONLY (alert/manager.py:96-97), and alert/helpers.py:52-61 builds it from those two and never reads audioAlerts. Decisively: `grep -rniE "mixer|aplay|playsound|winsound|espeak|paplay|beep" src/` returns ZERO hits -- there is no speaker code on the Pi to gate. So NO RESTART CAN EVER MAKE THAT ROW DO ANYTHING, and "no control silently no-ops" is unachievable BY WIRING. That is a product call, not an implementation: (a) drop the key from OVERRIDABLE_KEYS -- one line, and the row vanishes from the band, the write gate and the injected read at once, because US-530/531/532 all derive from that list on purpose; (b) RECOMMENDED -- keep the row with an honest 4th apply-state, "no effect -- not implemented", disclosing the no-op instead of hiding it; (c) scope audio as real work in its own story.

GENERALISABLE LESSON -- A CAPABILITY THE TESTS CANNOT SEE IS STILL A CAPABILITY. Every prior F-126 story closed on dev-box proof: real HTTP server, real config.json, real 401s. NONE of that can observe a PolicyKit denial, because polkit does not exist on the dev box. So an AC that depends on a Pi-side PRIVILEGE has to be validated by reading the grant chain (unit User= -> polkit rule -> app allow-list), not by running the suite. This is the same family as US-530's "a log line is a DECLARATION, not a mechanism": the code would have LOOKED like it restarts the service, and every test would have agreed with it.

READY TO BUILD THE MOMENT THE RULINGS LAND -- the other three controls have no judgment left in them, all verified this iteration: pi.power.mode -> genuinely LIVE, exactly as AC-3 asks. Today PowerModeProvider.fromConfig(self._config) (card_state_emitter.py:135) closes over the orchestrator's STARTUP config snapshot, so an overlay write never reaches the power tile. The fix is a drop-in on the seam US-421 built for precisely this (power_mode_provider.py:53-64 anticipates the swap): a PowerModeSource whose acquire() re-reads the effective value from disk each cycle, leaving provider, consumers and the honest-unknown contract untouched. pi.calibration.mode + pi.analysis.triggerAfterDrive -> honestly "applies on CAPTURE restart"; both are read once into a constructor at orchestrator start (calibration/manager.py:116-117, obdii/drive/detector.py:336-339), so "live" would be a lie and US-532's conservative label is already correct -- it only wants sharpening to name WHICH restart.

AND ONE DESIGN NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS US-533 UP: the apply-state should become a PYTHON SSOT pinned to the JS mirror in BOTH directions, not a JS-only field. Right now SETTINGS_SPECS (carousel.js:1110-1120) has JS asserting apply-semantics about PYTHON consumers with no drift guard. That is precisely the cross-language risk US-532 closed for the key list with test_settingsSpecsCoversTheOverlayAllowListExactly -- same shape, same fix -- and it is what stops a future consumer change from leaving a stale "applies now" behind.

NO HONESTY REGRESSION WHILE THIS SITS: US-532 shipped all 5 rows "applies on restart", which a restart always satisfies, so the deployed band is truthful today. That under-promise was built for exactly this situation -- waiting costs only time.

ENVIRONMENT (unchanged, re-confirmed): `make` is NOT on PATH -- `make lint` exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check` per touched file (TD-075 keeps project-wide ruff at exit 1 on a clean tree). Glob/ripgrep over the whole tree TIMES OUT on this SMB share -- scope greps to src/ or a subdir, or use `ls` via Bash. No .py/.js file was modified this iteration, so no lint gate applied.
